title: How long a reed lasts and trimming it
summary: A good reed lasts about a month; he sometimes cuts one down, as on his last job with Armstrong.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I forgot about how long does a reed last you if you get a good one?

Well, that depends. If a good reed will last me, I remember I think I used a reed practically a whole month. A whole month. Even playing almost every night. Yeah. Might last a month. Well, sometimes they're good and then they get real, real damp, real water soaked all the way. Then they get too soft. You see, then you got to change it.
Did you ever fool around with reeds? I guess everybody has a times like cutting them down or burning them like some of the fellas always do.

Yeah, yeah. Sometime you got a good reed and it's a little too soft. And if you can cut it down, sometime you get good results. But after once you bind them, they don't last too long. They won't last too long. I think I got to bind one on my planet, right? Now the last job I played up with Armstrong, I had to bind it. Because it was a little too soft.
